column9: TWIN of CM848 0x539938. Test used for pairs 1-3: every statement of the shorter function has a counterpart at the same position in the longer one, with the same constants, and the longer one only adds blocks. CM848 has 6 statements: completed power-down count + 1, queue the 2-byte EEPROM write, wait at most 1000 passes, power cycle sequence number = completed + incomplete, queue it, wait at most 1000 passes, then call the application main's restart entry through a register-loaded address. CM550 has all six in the same order, with 1000 and the same record offsets. It only adds blocks: the inline watchdog kicks, vp44_initVP44StatusMonitoring (it points the discrete-input override pointer and runs mc68k_sampleAndDebounceDiscreteInputs 4 times) and an interrupt mask that is restored before the jump. The per-pass delays are platform delays. The only hardware access is the watchdog kick, so the unprefixed shared name loses nothing.

The CM848 half of the twin with CM550 0x27af0, so it takes the same unprefixed name. Its six statements recur in CM550 in the same order and with the same constants: completed + 1, queue, wait at most 1000, sequence = completed + incomplete, queue, wait at most 1000, and a computed call into the main's restart entry (lis/addi 0x54d30 + blrl here, movea.l #0x28978 + jsr (a2) in CM550). Both firmwares use the same EEPROM record offsets and call it from the same three points of the power-down sequence and from the EEPROM save's 0x50-sample key check. CM550 adds only the watchdog kicks, the discrete-input re-initialization and an interrupt mask.

TWIN of CM848 0x4bd00. Both are the same dword copy loop from a ROM image to its RAM copy, testing first and running until the RAM end. Both have the same start-up slot: the application main calls each once, right after the working-RAM clear (pair 5) and right before run_location = NORMAL. In both firmwares the region is the one the RAM refresh keeps in step with ROM. CM550's cm550_canMemoryPointerTableInit (0x2e9f8) loads the refresh descriptor {0x80654a, 0x808acc, ROM 0x61376} and the RAM / ROM cursors. CM848's cm848_initializeRamRefresh (0x5389c4) loads {0x3feed0, 0x40a046, ROM 0x64aea} and sensor_cal_ram_write_ptr / sensor_cal_rom_read_ptr. CM550 adds only the inline watchdog kick per dword. The addresses and lengths (2401 dwords against about 11358) are memory-map constants and have to differ. 'Calibration' is the accurate word for both regions.

The CM848 half of the twin with CM550 0x117ec: the same dword copy loop, the same slot (after clearing RAM, before run_location = NORMAL) and the same role (filling the RAM calibration image that the RAM refresh then keeps in step with ROM 0x64aea). One thing for the applier: CM848 already has cm848_copyROMCalibrationToRAM (0x509b74). That function copies the J1939 NAMEs and source addresses, so its name is misleading, and after this rename the two names differ only in word order. Renaming 0x509b74 later would avoid the confusion; it does not block this row.

TWIN of CM848 0x538974. Both run the same chunked clear: test p < limit first, chunk end = p + 256 bytes, clamp the chunk end to the limit, clear dwords while p <= chunk end, repeat. That bound is inclusive in both, so each pass clears 260 bytes and the dword at the limit is cleared too. This shared quirk points to one source. Both have the same slot: the application main calls each once, as the first call after the TPU set-up. CM550 adds only the inline watchdog kick per chunk. The regions (CM550 0x800000-0x80def4, CM848 0x3fa000-0x41428e) are memory-map constants. clearWorkingRam is the more specific of the two existing names.

The CM848 half of the twin with CM550 0x2e9ac: the same 256-byte chunk clear with the same inclusive bound and clamp, called once as the application main's first call after the TPU set-up. CM550 adds only a watchdog kick per chunk. Same name, prefix dropped.

TWIN of CM848 0x204a8. Both run the same compare chain with the same constants: below 0x41, services 4 / 5 return 3 and 0x19 returns 5; 0x41-0x4e return the table byte at base + service; anything else returns 1. The 14 table bytes are identical. Each has one caller, its application's PGN 61184 response builder, which uses the result as the echo count. CM550's function_definitions.csv rows 217-218 carry the old name in column 2. The callers themselves (cm550_diagnosticMultiPacketResponseBuilder 0x3216a / cm848_sendJ1939ResponseFrame 0x249c4) look like a twin pair too: the same 0xef0000 header, 0x0c / 0x0d + code / 0x0e for 0xfe, lengths +1 / +2 / +3. That pair is a lead only, not proposed here.

The CM848 half of the twin with CM550 0xb688: the same compares, the same returns, the same 14-byte table and the same caller role (the application's PGN 61184 response builder, header 0xef0000). The boot kernel's cm848_getDiagnosticResponseEchoLength (0x3d54) is a third copy of the same code. Its table is at RAM 0x3f97bf + service, and the boot's cm848_sendDiagServiceResponse calls it (bl at 0x74c0, header 0xefff00). It keeps its cm848_ name, like cm848_getBootMemoryServiceHeaderLength next to the shared getJ1939MemoryServiceHeaderLength. A later consistency rename could make it cm848_getBootDiagnosticResponseEchoLength; that is not part of this row.

Both main_loop functions are the same thing, so one better shared name replaces the old one. Each is the periodic interrupt timer's handler: it runs one frame of a 40-phase executive and times it with the executive timing gatherer. It is not a loop, and the snake_case name also breaks the lowerCamelCase rule for functions. The CM550 one is the raw exception handler (movem save ... movem restore; rte) that the vector table points at. CM848's is a callback (blr) that the SIU dispatcher calls (see the CM848 row). The bodies have the same design. Phases 0-39 (0x27) wrap to 0, and the default case also sets 0. Every phase makes one common call, then alternates even and odd task sets, then calls rotating groups. The timing gatherer clears the 40 per-phase records when its enable switches on (total 0 / count 0 / minimum 0xffff / maximum 0 / overflow 0), takes the start time, updates maximum / minimum / total / count and the overflow counters after the phase, and steps the record pointer; phase 0 resets the pointer. The confidence rates that both are the same thing; the name is my choice (alternative: periodicExecutiveInterruptHandler). The old name survives in comments: 54 lines of the CM848 .cpp, 10 CM848 global comments and 9 CM848 function comments. It also survives in the phase globals main_loop_scheduler_phase (CM848 0x3fa008) and main_loop_iteration_counter / main_loop_phase_index / main_loop_reserved (CM550). Update them or add '(was main_loop)'.

The same thing as CM550's 0x1b876, so both take one new shared name (see the CM550 row for the design). Here it is the periodic interrupt timer's dispatched callback. The SIU interrupt dispatcher calls it from table entry 15, and it acknowledges the PIT itself by reading PISCR and writing the value back before its 40-phase switch. It times each frame into executive_frame_timings (e2m 12A6), and it ends with blr, so it is not a loop. Decoding PISCR = 0x105 as PIRQ level 7 (SIVEC code 0x3c, which is entry 15) comes from my recall of the MPC555 PISCR layout and only supports the table-entry evidence.

The function has no 'mode'. It dispatches a frame received on the chip select 5 82527 by message object number, and that controller carries the VP44 pump link. The low byte of its word argument is the message object number (interrupt code - 2). It handles exactly the three receive objects: object 1 calls 0x4025c(), then 0x4057e(&object 1 = 0xFFC810); object 3 calls 0x4073e(&object 3 = 0xFFC830); object 5 calls 0x40890(), then 0x408f6(&object 5 = 0xFFC850). All five handlers are in the undumped code above 0x40000. Prefix: vp44_, because the CS5 identifiers are the ECM <-> pump control module messages that the e2m files under its 'VP44 FSS' group (proof in the evidence). Not mc68k_: the body reads and writes no MC68336 or chip select register. It only adds 0x10 / 0x30 / 0x50 to the RAM pointer at 0x8000f0 and passes the result on; the device accesses happen in the undumped handlers. No CM848 twin exists (CM848 has TouCAN, no 82527, no VP44). Medium-confidence detail, kept out of the name: by identifier digit and image order, object 1 (0x112) is the pump-to-ECM 'cylinder event' message, object 3 (0x512) the 'RAM request' reply and object 5 (0x712) the 'security' message. The rename must also update function_definitions.csv:219, which keeps the current name and whose comment names the old wrapper name.

This is the receive branch of mc68k_canCs5InterruptHandler. For a message object whose interrupt fired and whose control 0 bit 5 (TXIE) is clear, the handler calls it with the object number. It passes the low byte of its word argument on, as a word, to the receive dispatcher (vp44_dispatchReceivedPumpMessage). Receive objects 1 / 3 / 5 are initialized with control 0 = 0x99 (bit 5 clear). Prefix: vp44_, the dispatcher's prefix, because its only caller is the CS5 (pump link) interrupt handler. It touches no register, so not mc68k_. Checked the caller: mc68k_canCs5InterruptHandler loops on the 82527 interrupt register 0xFFC85F. Codes 3..16 reach object code - 2: it writes 0xfd to that object's control 0 (resets IntPnd, keeps the other bit pairs), then tests bit 5. Codes 1 / 2 / >16 read CAN_CS5_STATUS and re-initialize only on bit 7 (bus off). Its name is right (it reads and writes CS5 registers), so no row for it. The CS4 handler has the same shape, and its wrappers cm550_serialNodeAddressForwarder / cm550_serialNodeAddressChecker (0x1e086 / 0x1e056) are misnamed the same way (out of scope). The rename must also update function_definitions.csv:333 (current name).

This is the transmit branch of mc68k_canCs5InterruptHandler. For a message object whose control 0 bit 5 (TXIE) is set, the handler calls it with the object number. It passes the low byte of its word argument on, as a word, to the empty transmit hook 0xc80c. The same bit-5-set branch in the CS4 handler leads to mc68k_canCs4TransmitNextFrame (the transmit-complete side), which fixes the polarity. As configured, no CS5 object has bit 5 set: the transmit objects 2 / 4 / 6 get control 0x5559 (control 0 = 0x55). So this branch runs only if the undumped transmit code enables a transmit interrupt, hence medium. Prefix: vp44_, because its only caller is the CS5 (pump link) interrupt handler. It touches no register. The rename must also update function_definitions.csv:332 (current name).

The body is one rts. Both of its callers are 82527 transmit-interrupt branches, and both push the message object number as a word. vp44_handleCanCs5TransmitInterrupt calls it for any CS5 object with TXIE set. The CS4 transmit branch (cm550_serialNodeAddressChecker) calls it for every object except the one at 0x80D9F4, whose transmit interrupt sends the next queued J1939 frame. It is the do-nothing transmit-complete hook. Named from position only, hence medium. Prefix: cm550_, generic, because the CS4 (J1939) path calls it too, so it is not VP44-only. It touches no register and has no CM848 twin. Both callers push a word, so a function_definitions row (0, message_object, ushort) would make the calls show the object number.

It decides whether the latest engine speed sensor pulse period ended on the sync pulse, the extra tooth. It runs only while the word 0x803d5c is set (1 in the RAM dump). The low byte of backup_sensor_flag picks the sensor. With 0 it uses the primary period 0x80d04a and the primary ring (start 0x80cd1e, next pointer 0x80cd08, last entry 0x80d078), and the threshold 0x8001a4. With a nonzero flag it uses the backup period 0x80d04e, ring 0x80ceae / 0x80cd0c / 0x80d07c, and threshold 0x8001a0. Above CSCKES (0x807ed8, e2m 100B +30 'RPM above which the engine is considered running'; 300 rpm in the dump), the result is 1 when the period is below the threshold. While cranking, cm550_bufferThresholdValidator confirms a short period. In a cold crank (coolant 0x80a336 below CSCDCKTP 0x807c0e and speed at or below CSCDESTR 0x807c16), cm550_bufferDecreasingPatternCheck can still find the pulse with its slope test. The function then sets the next threshold to period x CSXT_1PC (0x807c1e, e2m 11A7 +10 'VALUE USED TO DETECT SYNC PULSE'; 192/256 = 75 % in the dump) >> 8. The result goes to 0x80aa16 (primary) or 0x80aa18 (backup). The phase comparators skip their main / backup edge compare when it is set. Nothing here reads retarder data. It touches no MC68336 register, so the prefix is cm550_. Twin verdict: this is a counterpart, not a twin. CM848 detects the additional cam pulse inside the TPU-A PMA function (mpc555_handleCamSignalInterrupt reads the channel status), its CHR e2m has none of the CSXT / CSCK records, and its Cam_Sync_State has 5 values against CM550's CMSYSS 0 / 1 / 2. Apply note: rename function_definitions.csv rows 224-225 too. They are matched by address, but the name column must agree or the build warns. Leads (not applied): 0x8001a4 / 0x8001a0 (anc_altitude_table_3_size / anc_altitude_table_2_ptr) are the primary / backup sync pulse thresholds. 0x8001a8 / 0x8001ac / 0x8001b0 / 0x8001b4 are the latest period and the previous-entry / ring-start / ring-end pointers. 0x80ccf2 (fuel_demand_blend_mode_select) is the engine speed compared with CSCKES. 0x10394 cm550_canBusTimingInit only initializes both thresholds (nothing CAN). 0x101b8 / 0x1011c are the cranking confirmation and the cold crank slope test.

This is the primary speed sensor period processor for speed_measurement_mode 3, the wheel with a sync pulse. It is the only work function of mc68k_tpuChannel10PrimarySpeedInterruptHandlerMode3. It stores the TPU channel 10 period and edge time (0x80d04a / 0x80d052), then asks cm550_detectEngineSpeedSensorSyncPulse(0) whether the period ended on the sync pulse. On a sync pulse: - If the periods since the last sync pulse (0x800658) equal Period_Meas_Per_Cam (0x807ec0, 24 in the dump), CMSYSS (0x80d0cc, e2m 11A8 CAM_SYNC_STATE) becomes 1, HAVE SYNC. - Otherwise HAVE becomes 2, LOST. Below CSCKES the sync loss count 0x80d0d2 (e2m 11A8 +6 CSERCU 'TOTAL NUMBER OF SYNC LOSSES') counts up to the limit 0x807f2a. Otherwise the cam sync error (status word 2 bit 0x800 and its first-occurrence latch) is set. - The short period is kept in 0x800660 and the count restarts at 0. On a normal tooth: - The count goes up by 1. - The first period after a sync pulse gets the kept part added, which rebuilds the split tooth period, and the tooth counter 0x80ccea restarts. Too many teeth while in sync means LOST. - It then does the same pulse period ring, per-cam sum, per-cylinder window and accumulator updates that the mode 0 / 1 / 2 handlers do inline, plus the fault heal. It reloads the main lost-sensor timeout and returns the periods since the sync pulse. The handler re-arms channel 10 on 0 while in sync. No other mode detects a sync pulse, hence 'WithSyncPulse'. Nothing here reads throttle data. It touches no MC68336 register (the handler reads the TPU), so the prefix is cm550_. Twin verdict: this is a counterpart, not a twin, of CM848's mpc555_handleCamSignalInterrupt. That function drives a 5-state cam sync from the TPU-A PMA status and never merges a split period. The dumped ECU runs mode 1 (RAM 0x808F04 = 0x00019E90). Apply notes: rename function_definitions.csv rows 256-258. The split 0x1a95e (vp44FaultThresholdTablesInit) is not a function. Remove its function_renames.csv row (line 257) and add 0x0001a95e to deleted_functions.csv, following the 0x00015e06 precedent. A deletion while the renames row is still there gets recreated by the import. No CM848 row uses that name. Leads (not applied): 0x80d04a io_control_handshake_state is the primary pulse period (its e2m neighbor 0x80d04e is EPS_Period_Backup). 0x800658 sync_miss_counter is the pulse periods since the sync pulse. 0x80d0d2 crank_sync_error_counter is CSERCU. 0x80d078 / 0x80d07c / 0x80d080 (eps_control_mode_param_1 / _3, eps_override_output_state) are ring pointers.

Each call runs one step of the start-up test of the PWM 3 and PWM 4 output drivers (CTM4 PWMSM7 / PWMSM8). mc68k_monitorPwmOutputReadBackFaults calls it during its first 6 passes. The pass counter 0x80dc60 is only incremented, and nothing in the dumped ROM re-arms it. - Pass 1: each output whose enable bit is set (0x4 / 0x8 of 0x805ffe, e2m 11E9 commanded enables) is driven at 100 % duty. PWM7A:PWM7B and PWM8A:PWM8B are loaded with period : period, from the e2m 11E5 period words 0x80899c / 0x80899e in microseconds x 8 counts. A disabled output gets 0 %. - Passes 3 and 5: each output's PIN bit (bit 7 of PWM7SIC / PWM8SIC) is compared with its read-back on SIM_PORTF0 bit 1 / bit 2. A mismatch sets the PWM 3 / PWM 4 driver error flags (status word 7 bits 0x40 / 0x80 and their first-occurrence latches). Agreement heals them. Both outputs then go to 0 %. - Passes 2, 4 and 6 do nothing. These are the only setters of the two fault bits in the ROM. mc68k_pwmFuelDemandOutputCalculator writes the PWM 3 / 4 duty requests only after the counter passes 5. Nothing here reads a water-in-fuel input. The function accesses CTM4 and SIM port F registers, so the mc68k_ prefix stays. Twin verdict: no twin. The MPC555 has no CTM4 or port F, and CM848 checks output read-backs through its driver table (cm848_updateOutputReadBackFaultBits).

This is the start-up set-up of the discrete outputs. mc68k_applicationMain calls it once, right after the discrete inputs are primed (0x15dd0 vp44_initVP44StatusMonitoring). It is a direct call, not a pointer: ROM 0x2870a is that jsr's operand. 1. It writes the default output states into the output images at 0x80bcf6..0x80bcfb. Each write happens only when no client holds that output's override slot (0x80bd1a + n). 2. It configures the chip select 2 output driver: registers 8 / 9 / 10 = 0x0F / 0x80 / 0x80, output port 1 (0xFFD004) cleared, port 2 bit 7 (0xFFD006) cleared. 3. It sets TPU channel 13 to function 0xE with PARAM0 = 0x113 and runs a handshake. HSR 2, then it waits for PARAM1 bit 15 = 0. HSR 1, then it waits for 1. HSR 2, then it waits for 0. Then it sets port 2 bit 7 and issues HSR 1. 4. It ends with mc68k_ioDriverStrobeHandler, which writes ports 1 and 2 and port E from the images. That handler drives channel 13 from bit 5 of 0x80bcfb: set gives HSR 2, clear gives HSR 1. That bit is the fuel shut-off (FSO) command. cm550_fuelDemandLimitSelector11 sets and clears it from fso_state_desired_from_fuel_system_specific_algorithms, and e2m DRFSEA (block E +2D, mask 0x20) is 'CONTROLS FUEL SHUT OFF DRIVER'. So channel 13 is most likely the FSO driver output. That stays out of the name because none of these e2m files is J90350's own. The meaning of port 2 bit 7 is not settled: the e2m versions disagree on E +29 bit 7. The function accesses the TPU and the chip select 2 device, so the mc68k_ prefix stays. Twin verdict: no twin. CM848 has no chip select 2 device and no TPU channel 13 handshake; its outputs go through the SIU / MIOS / TPU-B / QSPI drivers. Lead (not applied): 0x15dd0 vp44_initVP44StatusMonitoring is the discrete input initialization (the override mask pointer, then 4 passes of mc68k_sampleAndDebounceDiscreteInputs). It does not monitor VP44 status.

ASKED ITEM. Twin of CM848 0x216fc cm848_restartThroughBootRom, so it takes one shared unprefixed name (the CM848 row is the next change). The differences come first. (a) Link cases: CM550 has a body in case 1 (the J1708 diagnostic message queue, 0xb6e8) and an empty case 2 (cmpi.b #2 with no branch). CM848 has an empty case 1 and a body in case 2 (the SCI byte). Case 0, the J1939 response frame to the request, is the same in both. (b) The hardware step between the long delay and the interrupt mask: CM550 turns bit 4 of the output byte 0x80bcf8 off unless 0x80bd2e is set, then writes the outputs with mc68k_ioDriverStrobeHandler; CM848 sets chip select 0 (BR0 / OR0) and SIUMCR. (c) The vector address (ROM 0x8 / ROM 0x104) and the delay units. Everything else is the same steps in the same order: the engine state 1 (STOPPED) gate, else 7 (CM848 J1939_DIAGNOSTIC_RESULT_NOT_SAFE); drain the EEPROM write queue; save the key-on hour meter, then the engine hour meter, 4 bytes each, each followed by a poll of its EEPROM mirror word while ram_refresh_enable is on (a short fixed delay while it is off); acknowledge; long delay; mask interrupts; SP to the stack top; jump through the boot ROM's restart vector; 0xff. The delays keep a 2 : 1 : 200 ratio (CM550 500 / 250 / 50000 ticks, CM848 19 / 9 / 1953, which is trunc(CM550 / 25.6) for all three). The role is the same: J1939 diagnostic service 11's handler calls it with (request, 0) in both firmwares, from the same 8-service registrar. FALLBACK if the reviewer reads (a) / (b) as 'the code differs': cm550_restartThroughBootRom, with CM848 left as it is. Its own accesses are RAM, the ROM vector, SR and SP, with no MC68336 module register, so the prefix would be cm550_, not mc68k_. APPLY: rename the name column of CM550 function_definitions.csv rows 226-228 (0x1192a); update the comment of 0x34bf8 mc68k_delayTimeBaseTicksWithWatchdogService2, which names cm550_FUN_0001192a. Suggested plate: Software restart into the boot ROM without a hardware reset (twin of CM848 0x216fc, shared name). Only in engine state 1 (STOPPED), else 7. It waits for the EEPROM write queue, saves the key-on hour meter (0x80bda4 -> EEPROM 0x34) and the engine hour meter (0x80ccee -> EEPROM 0x46), and acknowledges on acknowledge_datalink (0 = J1939 response frame to request / 1 = J1708 diagnostic message queue / 2 = none). It then waits 50000 ticks, turns output bit 4 of 0x80bcf8 off (unless 0x80bd2e is set) and writes the outputs, masks interrupts, sets SP to 0x811000 and jumps through ROM 0x8 to the boot block's warm entry 0x3abe.

ASKED ITEM (the CM848 half of the 0x1192a twin rename): a twin takes one unprefixed name in both firmwares. If the CM550 row falls back to cm550_restartThroughBootRom, drop this row. APPLY: these CM848 texts name it and need updating: function_renames.csv comments of 0x218b0 (cm848_restartThroughBootRomAfterSciRequest), 0x218dc (cm848_handleJ1939RestartService) and 0x522074 (cm848_sciTransmitSingleByteOne); enums.csv J1939_DIAGNOSTIC_SERVICE 0x0b and J1939_DIAGNOSTIC_RESULT 0x07 comments; firmware/CLAUDE.md's serial reflash hand-off bullet. This function has no function_definitions.csv row. Fix one phrase of its plate with the rename: it says it waits for each hour meter 'while a diagnostic session is active', but the code waits while ram_refresh_enable is on (lhz 0x40c04a at 0x21770 / 0x217d4; 0 = a fixed li r3,9 delay instead).

ASKED ITEM. This is the application main's restart entry: a point in mc68k_applicationMain's tail that has its own function row. cm550_restartOnKeyOnDuringPowerDown jumps to it. It re-runs the main's last six initializations, sets SP back to 0x811000, clears power_down_start_flag (0x80d0ca), enables interrupts, runs the background idle loop until power_down_start_flag is set, then masks interrupts, makes two power-down calls and calls mc68k_runPowerDownSequence. It never returns. Counterpart, not a twin, of CM848 0x54d30 cm848_restartApplicationWithoutReset: the skeleton is the same, but the init calls differ (6 against 4), the loop body differs (CM550's idle delay counter against cm848_refreshRamCalibration) and the post-run calls differ (2 against 5). So it takes the CM848 vocabulary with CM550's own prefix. cm550_, not mc68k_: its own accesses are RAM words, SR and SP, with no MC68336 module or chip select register (round 85's hardware_access_kinds.py rule). The .cpp hides most of this. The decompiler folds the just-cleared 0x80d0ca to 0, so it drops the SP set, the loop test and the exit block 0x289ea ('Removing unreachable block'). That is also why mc68k_runPowerDownSequence shows no caller. Naming 0x80d0ca does not change this; the word would have to be treated as volatile. APPLY: the comments of 0x27af0 cm550_restartOnKeyOnDuringPowerDown and 0x284e8 mc68k_applicationMain mention 'the restart entry 0x28978' and can name it. Suggested plate: The restart entry of mc68k_applicationMain, reached from cm550_restartOnKeyOnDuringPowerDown (movea.l #0x28978,a2 / jsr (a2)). It re-runs the main's last six initializations, sets SP to 0x811000, clears power_down_start_flag, enables interrupts (andi #0xf0ff,sr) and runs the background loop until power_down_start_flag is set. It then masks interrupts (ori #0x700,sr) and calls 0x445fc, cm550_writeHourMeterConversionData and mc68k_runPowerDownSequence. It never returns. CM848's counterpart is cm848_restartApplicationWithoutReset.

ASKED ITEM. e2m 10C7 +4 Parameter_Block_Uploaded [SSPBUL] 'Number indicating which parameter block was uploaded at powerup, 0=none'. CM550's own parameter ID table proves the placement: block 10C7 -> 0x80dc6c and the next block, 1010, at 0x80dc72, so 10C7 is exactly ram_refresh_enable / 0x80dc6e / 0x80dc70. The code agrees: 0 none / 1 / 2 is the flash parameter block the RAM copy 0x804F96-0x806549 came from at power-up (the loaders) or was last saved to (the savers). The power-down sequence saves into the other block, the RAM refresh compares the copy's tail word with that block, and 0 turns the RAM refresh off and sets a fault at start-up. 'calibration bank' was the wrong vocabulary (round 85 lead). Working RAM, so no _cal. Word by every access; the untyped row renders as _calibration_bank_active. CM848's 10C7 +4 (0x40c04e) has no row, since CM848 has no flash parameter blocks.

ASKED ITEM. e2m 1069 Powerdown_Memory_Save_Start [SDSVSR] 'Count indicating the number of times powerdown memory save has started': the start count of flash parameter block 1's power-down save. The block 1 saver bumps it by 1, or by 2, so that its sum with the block 2 start count ends odd (block 1 newest). It waits for that EEPROM write before it erases block 0x4000. After the program and the checksum it copies the count into the complete count 0x803fd8. The start-up selector (0x114d4) compares the two: start != complete means block 1's last save never finished. Placement: CM550's parameter ID table puts block 1069 at EEPROM 0x4ca (0x803fd4) and block 106A at EEPROM 0x4e0 (0x803fea). So CM550's 1069 is one word longer than CM848's. Its +0 word 0x803fd4 is unused (0 in the EEPROM, no access; the table's old CM550 label calls it a blank spot replacing the key-off count), and every CM848 1069 record sits 2 bytes later in CM550: SDSVSR is at +2 = 0x803fd6, and SDFHFXFG at +14 = 0x803fe8, the last word before 106A in both firmwares. The saves run only at power-down: savePowerDownDataToFlashBank is the savers' only caller. EEPROM mirror (0x803b0a-0x804155), so _cal. Word; the untyped row renders as _calibration_bank1_write_sequence.

ASKED ITEM. e2m 1069 Powerdown_Memory_Save_Start_2 [SDSVSR02] 'Counts number of times powerdown block 2 save has started', at CM550 1069 +A (CM848 +8; the one-word shift is explained in the 0x803fd6 row). The block 2 saver bumps it so the sum with the block 1 start count ends even (block 2 newest), waits for it, erases block 0x6000, programs it, writes the checksum (EEPROM 0xA) and then copies it into the complete count 0x803fe0.
